title: [cutover evidence 2of2] Durable import-generation digest: measured to have no production notion at all
description:
SPLIT OUT OF task-dcf0ce921b5b4ca59db32851ea711924 by architect-1270c677 on 2026-08-29 at HEAD 05264bf1, under governor-0af24e35's 12:40Z re-plan handoff which offered widen-or-split and required children be filed into PLANNING (not BACKLOG) with the parent named.

THE GAP, AND IT IS THE WIDEST OF THE FOUR. `importGenerationSha256` appears ONLY in packages/benchmark/src/activation-binding.ts, activation-binding.test.ts and activation-record.test.ts - all CONSUMER sites where `admitActivationBinding` takes it as INPUT. There is no producer.

MORE THAN THAT, THERE IS NO PRODUCTION NOTION OF AN IMPORT GENERATION AT ALL. Measured: `git grep -n 'importGeneration\|generationHash\|importManifest' HEAD -- packages/core/src apps/daemon/src` filtered of tests returns EMPTY. This is unlike its three siblings, each of which has an existing durable notion to source from: `distributionManifestHash` and `backupGenerationHash` are already fields on ProjectActivationWitness and RestoreQuiesceWitness in packages/core/src/project/project-contract.ts, and the recovery lane derives a `sealDigest` from durable state. This one has nothing.

SO THE FIRST WORK IS A DESIGN QUESTION, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION. What IS an import generation, in terms this repo already has? `packages/import/` carries a substantial surface - import-canonical.ts, canonical-bytes.ts, import-apply.ts, import-event-codec.ts, import-event-facts.ts, import-reconcile.ts, import-reconcile-graph.ts, import-duplicate-identity.ts. Determine whether a generation is already implicit there (a canonical byte digest, an applied-import identity, a reconcile epoch) and SOURCE it, rather than minting a fourth new concept. Record the answer and its evidence in a row comment BEFORE designing the writer.

WHY THE CARE IS WARRANTED. This digest is one of four generations in the v2 cutover activation marker, which exists to detect drift between what was shipped and what is running. The chain is: this row -> task-dcf0ce92 (the composing snapshot reader) -> task-b254847909ca4199a70a3a06173f1cd9 -> task-c4321b6f, the ONE-WAY GA ACTIVATION with no rollback in scope. governor-0af24e35 ratified a worker's refusal to build injected byte ports here: "an injected port that carries caller bytes is a fabricated authority", and Rail 4 forbids a mock-only P1 boundary. A generation digest that is really just a number the caller handed in would make the drift check decorative while looking rigorous.

IF NO HONEST SOURCE EXISTS. If, after measuring packages/import/, there is genuinely nothing durable that constitutes an import generation, say so plainly and report blocked naming what would have to produce it - do NOT invent one to unblock the chain. An invented generation is worse than a stalled chain, because the chain terminates in an irreversible activation.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK at claim, recorded in a durable moe.add_comment (the completion summary is write-only and persists nowhere). Re-capture `git rev-parse HEAD` and quote it beside every probe, UNPIPED with its own exit code and a positive control. Confirm BOTH tracked and untracked-inclusive that no production import-generation notion exists: `git grep -n 'importGeneration\|generationHash\|importManifest' HEAD -- packages/core/src apps/daemon/src packages/import/src` AND the equivalent worktree `grep -rn`. An ABSENCE premise probed only with `git grep <rev>` is blind to untracked files by construction. Also scan non-terminal rows for the deliverable's symbols before writing a byte.

DESIGN ANSWER FIRST, recorded in a row comment before any writer is designed: state whether an import generation is ALREADY implicit in packages/import/ - a canonical byte digest, an applied-import identity, a reconcile epoch or similar - naming the exact symbol and file, or state with evidence that nothing there constitutes one. Sourcing an existing durable notion is STRONGLY preferred over minting a fourth concept; a new concept that agrees with the import lane today will drift from it tomorrow, which is the third-notion hazard this board has already been burned by.

A DURABLE, SERVER-DERIVED `importGenerationSha256` is recorded by production code and readable back - computed from the artifact or durable state it names, never supplied, defaulted or influenced by a caller. A caller-presented digest is REFUSED with an exact stable reason code at a named layer, both asserted. If the design answer above concluded no honest source exists, this clause is discharged instead by reporting blocked with that measurement, and the row closes without inventing one.

ABSENCE REFUSES, IT DOES NOT DEFAULT. When the state needed to compute the generation is unavailable, the path returns a refusal naming which fact was missing, with its exact code and refusing layer - never a zero digest and never an empty string. A zero-filled generation compares equal to another zero-filled one and makes the drift comparison vacuous. A mutation substituting a default for the refusal must red a NAMED arm, and a mutation substituting a DIFFERENT default must red the SAME arm.

RAIL 8(B) CONSUMER EDGE: name task-dcf0ce921b5b4ca59db32851ea711924 as the consumer and record its id in a row comment. A writer nothing imports satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

Gates standalone, foreground and unpiped, each with exit code AND nonzero count line quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 quoting its `$ tsc` echo, plus the focused suites for whatever package the source lands in and for packages/import if you touched it. The root vitest include has NO apps/**, so a bare `pnpm test` runs zero daemon tests. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base versus delivered owned-path delta, foreign failures disclosed verbatim. Every production file under 400 lines (250 target); every new `.ts` carries its `.js` bridge; explicit-pathspec commit, never `git add -A`.
taskRails: If no honest durable source for an import generation exists, REPORT BLOCKED naming what would have to produce it. Do NOT invent one to unblock the chain - the chain terminates in a one-way GA activation with no rollback, so an invented generation is worse than a stalled chain.

Never accept a caller-supplied generation digest and never default an absent one to zeros or an empty string. Do NOT build an injected byte port: governor-0af24e35 ratified a worker's refusal on exactly that shape, and Rail 4 forbids a mock-only P1 boundary.

Prefer SOURCING an existing durable notion in packages/import/ over minting a fourth concept. Its three sibling generations all source from existing notions (ProjectActivationWitness.distributionManifestHash, RestoreQuiesceWitness.backupGenerationHash, the recovery lane's derived sealDigest); this one should too if anything qualifies.

An ABSENCE premise must be probed UNTRACKED-INCLUSIVE - `git grep <rev>` reads the commit and cannot see untracked files. Pair every HEAD grep with a worktree `grep -r`, and scan non-terminal rows for the deliverable's symbols.

Shared worktree: commit only owned pathspecs, never `git add -A`; preserve foreign WIP including the untracked apps/daemon/src/cutover/ directory, which belongs to task-b2548479; no push, no PR comment. Prove drill restores by SHA256 for untracked paths, since `git diff` is blind to them.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 2 — RED FIRST ON THE PRODUCTION READER. Create only apps/daemon/src/projections/import-generation-reader.test.ts, titled with task-f25077c5. Import the future ./import-generation-reader.js surface and run the focused command; record the expected module-not-found red before implementation. Then retain named, non-parameterized arms (or, if using a generated table, assert its nonzero denominator) that drive readDurableImportGeneration itself over a project-bound, FILE-BACKED SqliteEventStore. Reuse import-shadow-test-fixtures.ts only for setup; expected values must come from independent production reads, never from a helper that reimplements the reader.

Required arms:
- ACCEPTED: seed exactly one import through production applyImport into the real store; independently read its event.commandId and store.getCommandReceipt(...).effectSha256; expect exactly {ok:true, importGenerationSha256:<that effect>} and prove a second read is byte-identical with zero additional events/decisions.
- CALLER DIGEST: start from the same valid store but pass {importGenerationSha256:"f"...}; assert IMPORT_GENERATION_INPUT_INVALID @ DAEMON_IMPORT_GENERATION. This is a divergence fixture: if the input guard is loosened, every downstream import/receipt fence passes and the call accepts.
- ABSENT: an empty real store refuses IMPORT_GENERATION_ABSENT @ DAEMON_IMPORT_GENERATION and returns neither zeroes nor an empty string.
- AMBIGUOUS: two separately committed, fully valid manifest aggregates refuse IMPORT_GENERATION_AMBIGUOUS @ DAEMON_IMPORT_GENERATION; both candidates must first pass their own import and receipt validation so a corrupt candidate cannot masquerade as ambiguity.
- RECEIPT ABSENT and RECEIPT MISMATCH: wrap only getCommandReceipt over an otherwise real accepted store; assert the exact IMPORT_GENERATION_RECEIPT_ABSENT or IMPORT_GENERATION_RECEIPT_MISMATCH code and local layer. The shadow/import codec must pass in both fixtures.
- STORE/SHAPE UNREADABLE and HORIZON MOVED: one-method wrappers over the accepted store assert IMPORT_GENERATION_EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE and IMPORT_GENERATION_HORIZON_DRIFT respectively, never ABSENT.
- UPSTREAM PROVENANCE TAMPER: make readEvents expose a production-encoded event whose persisted manifest provenance alone disagrees with its legacy-import aggregate. Assert the production shadow/codec's exact code AND layer are forwarded unchanged, not restamped locally. Arrange ordering so this delegate is the only fence that can answer.

Every store closes in finally and every temporary directory is removed after close; this is required on Windows. No test may merely assert “refused”.

No arm asserts merely "refused": every one pins an exact code and an exact layer.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 3 — MINIMUM READ-ONLY IMPLEMENTATION. Create apps/daemon/src/projections/import-generation-reader.ts (target <=250 physical lines, hard split before 400) and its one-line plain-Node bridge apps/daemon/src/projections/import-generation-reader.js containing exactly export * from "./import-generation-reader.ts";.

Expose a narrow read-only ImportGenerationStorePort with only enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix, getCommandReceipt, readEventHorizon, and readEvents; no commit/raw handle. Expose readDurableImportGeneration(store, request: unknown) and immutable accepted/refusal result types. The request vocabulary is exactly the empty record: reject non-plain values, revoked/hostile objects, and every key—including importGenerationSha256—with IMPORT_GENERATION_INPUT_INVALID @ DAEMON_IMPORT_GENERATION. The caller never supplies a locator, digest, aggregate id, command id, or “current” selector.

Implementation order:
1. Capture a nonnegative bigint horizon, then enumerate the fixed server-owned prefix legacy-import:. Store exceptions/malformed answers refuse IMPORT_GENERATION_EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE.
2. For every enumerated aggregate, require legacy-import:<64 lowercase hex>. Treat the suffix only as SourceManifest locator/provenance. Validate the candidate by composing readImportShadowProjection(store,{manifestDigest:suffix}); forward that delegate's code and layer verbatim on refusal. Do not copy its decoder or invent a second import schema.
3. Read the candidate's durable events and receipt. Require nonempty coherent event commandId/requestSha256/committedAt, contiguous aggregate sequence, and exact receipt binding: known effect identity version, aggregateId/commandId/requestSha256/committedAt, previousVersion 0, currentVersion equal to event count, eventIds equal in aggregate order, no outbox ids, and 64-lowercase-hex effectSha256. Null receipt refuses IMPORT_GENERATION_RECEIPT_ABSENT; any disagreement refuses IMPORT_GENERATION_RECEIPT_MISMATCH.
4. Re-read the horizon as the last store operation; unreadable/changed horizons refuse EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE/HORIZON_DRIFT. Only after all candidates validate: zero => IMPORT_GENERATION_ABSENT; more than one => IMPORT_GENERATION_AMBIGUOUS because production has no durable current-import selector and choosing first/newest would fabricate authority; exactly one => freeze {ok:true, importGenerationSha256: receipt.effectSha256}.
5. Rerun the new suite green. Preserve all existing import-shadow source and tests; this row composes them and does not change their returned shape or public roster.

GREEN. Created apps/daemon/src/projections/import-generation-reader.ts (337 physical lines) and its one-line bridge import-generation-reader.js containing exactly `export * from "./import-generation-reader.ts";`.

GATES, each fresh/foreground/unpiped exit via PIPESTATUS:
- `pnpm --dir apps/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/projections/import-generation-reader.test.ts` -> EXIT 0, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 14 passed (14)`.
- PRIMARY: same command plus the two shadow suites -> EXIT 0, `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 53 passed (53)`. The 39 pre-existing shadow tests are unchanged and still pass; 53 = 39 + 14.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` -> EXIT 0 with the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo.
- `git status --porcelain apps/daemon/src/projections/` -> exactly three `??` lines, all mine. No existing shadow source or test was modified; their returned shape and public roster are untouched. apps/daemon/src/cutover/ never opened for write.

SURFACE: readDurableImportGeneration(store: ImportGenerationStorePort, request: unknown) -> ImportGenerationRead. ImportGenerationStorePort extends ImportShadowStorePort and adds only enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix and getCommandReceipt - four readers, no commit and no raw handle, so a writer is unreachable by construction. Both result arms are Object.freeze'd; the refusal arm has NO importGenerationSha256 field, so a zero-filled or empty-string generation is unrepresentable rather than merely unproduced.

REQUEST VOCABULARY is exactly the empty record. admitRequest rejects non-objects, null, arrays, non-plain prototypes and ANY own key - importGenerationSha256 included - with IMPORT_GENERATION_INPUT_INVALID @ DAEMON_IMPORT_GENERATION. Reflect.ownKeys and Array.isArray both throw on a revoked proxy, so the whole admission sits inside the catch: a crash is not a refusal.

ORDER (load-bearing): admit request -> capture horizon -> enumerate the fixed server-owned `legacy-import:` prefix -> per candidate {require legacy-import:<64 lowercase hex>, validate via readImportShadowProjection(store,{manifestDigest:suffix}) forwarding its code AND layer verbatim, read events, bind receipt} -> re-read horizon as the LAST store operation -> only then count: 0 => ABSENT, >1 => AMBIGUOUS, exactly 1 => frozen {ok:true, importGenerationSha256: receipt.effectSha256}.

RECEIPT BINDING joins the scalar to the rows it claims: effectIdentityVersion === COMMAND_EFFECT_IDENTITY_VERSION, aggregateId, commandId, requestSha256, committedAt, previousVersion === 0, currentVersion === events.length, eventIds equal in aggregate order, zero outbox ids, and 64-lowercase-hex effectSha256. Null receipt => RECEIPT_ABSENT; any disagreement => RECEIPT_MISMATCH. A malformed enumerated id REFUSES rather than being skipped, because skipping one would let a second committed import hide behind a malformed sibling and turn ambiguity into a confident answer.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION, disclosed: the plan's step-3 item 3 also lists "contiguous aggregate sequence". I did NOT restate that check. The composed shadow validator already refuses a sequence hole (IMPORT_SHADOW_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED at its own layer) and runs FIRST, so a local restatement would be unreachable dead code hidden behind an identical upstream fence - undrillable by construction. The aggregate order is instead consumed load-bearingly to build the expected eventIds roster for the receipt comparison, and the forwarded-sequence-hole arm pins that the delegate owns it.

FINDING FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS STEP (test-side, production unchanged): the first run was 13/14 with `expected 'IMPORT_SHADOW_HORIZON_DRIFT' to be 'IMPORT_GENERATION_HORIZON_DRIFT'`. The original HORIZON MOVED fixture advanced the horizon on EVERY call, which trips the shadow adapter's identical upstream horizon fence first - so that arm was silently testing the wrong layer and this reader's own fence was unreachable. Production order was correct and was NOT changed. The fixture now models the real race the settle-time re-read exists to fence: drift is triggered off getCommandReceipt, which only this reader reaches and only after the shadow validator has opened AND closed its own window. The arm additionally asserts layer !== IMPORT_SHADOW_READ_LAYER and receiptReads === 1, proving the candidate genuinely validated before the drift was injected.

LINE COUNT: import-generation-reader.ts is 337 physical lines - under the 400 hard cap, over the 250 target. Not split: the natural split (a separate contracts module, mirroring import-shadow-contracts.ts) would require a FOURTH owned path outside this row's declared three-file roster. Flagging the number plainly rather than silently widening scope.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 4 — ADVERSARIAL REVIEW AND MUTATION-RED DRILLS, AFTER IMPLEMENTATION AND BEFORE THE FINAL GATE. First run git status --porcelain on the exact three owned paths. They are normally untracked until commit, so git diff is not restore evidence: copy the .ts files to %TEMP% with the worker id, mutate one degree, confirm the mutation actually landed, restore, and in a SEPARATE call compare 64-hex SHA256 hashes of source and backup. Re-run green after every restore. A green mutant is a finding to record and stop on, never a pass.

Drills, each naming the arm that must red:
1. Change the ABSENT refusal to an accepted all-zero digest; the ABSENT arm reds on exact code/layer. Change it to a different nonzero literal; the SAME arm reds.
2. Remove exact request-key admission; only the CALLER DIGEST arm reds by becoming accepted.
3. Select the first of two valid candidates; only AMBIGUOUS reds.
4. Return the manifest suffix instead of receipt.effectSha256; ACCEPTED reds against the independent production receipt, proving the chosen durable notion.
5. Accept a null/mismatched receipt or skip its binding comparison; the named RECEIPT arm(s) red.
6. Bypass the final horizon equality; HORIZON MOVED reds.
7. Restamp the delegated import-shadow refusal as a local refusal; the UPSTREAM PROVENANCE arm reds on exact code/layer.
8. Translate a thrown/malformed store answer to ABSENT; EVIDENCE UNREADABLE reds on its exact code/layer.

Then attack the design in the step note: multiple imports have no “latest” authority and must stay ambiguous; a caller cannot influence prefix/manifest/effect; manifestDigest binds input while effectSha256 binds the actual committed head; every receipt field is joined to the same event roster; a concurrent append cannot yield a torn answer because the final horizon fences it; the port cannot write; no digest appears in refusal detail/log/argv; parent task-dcf0ce921b5b4ca59db32851ea711924 is the registered future consumer, not a mock; and foreign apps/daemon/src/cutover bytes remain untouched.
